answer: Timed whisper intervals. Each new identity transmits a brief whisper beacon on a randomized schedule, and the kernel verifies that arrival timing matches its declared clock drift. The orchard of active identities is sampled continuously; mismatched intervals flag clones. Enforcement: identities whose timing variance falls below the natural noise floor are throttled. An attacker pays per-identity clock calibration and continuous idle upkeep to fake drift, scaling linearly with fleet size.
